item.title: Hecla Mining highlights US$ 483.5 million cash position in corporate presentation

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hecla Mining Company released a corporate presentation outlining a medium-term plan to lift silver output above 20 Moz. Silver production guidance set at 15.1-16.1 Moz for 2026, supported by Greens Creek, Lucky Friday, Keno Hill. Growth pipeline centered on Keno Hill ramp-up to 440 tpd, Midas restart, Greens Creek processing and tailings projects. Cash position reported at USD 483.5 million as of June 30, 2026; no long-term debt shown. Dividend maintained at USD 0.00375 per share, paid quarterly. item.title: Daimler Truck showcases new Fleetboard digital fleet management tools at IAA Transportation 2026
item.description: At IAA Transportation 2026, Daimler Truck outlined a revamped digital fleet-management offering built around a tighter, integrated vehicle-to-portal ecosyst
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At IAA Transportation 2026, Daimler Truck outlined a revamped digital fleet-management offering built around a tighter, integrated vehicle-to-portal ecosystem. Fleetboard will merge 12 products into five packages, spanning fleet operations, analytics, compliance, charging management, Uptime diagnostics. New My TruckPoint Store will sell Fleetboard services online, including standalone Mercedes-Benz Trucks Uptime without a service contract. From January 2027 production, selected Fleetboard services will be bundled for 36 months on most new diesel trucks, electric vehicles. TruckLive will split into Core and Plus from December 2026; Core stays free, Plus free for three years then paid. item.title: i-nest capital’s Fund II boosts assets under management to about JPY 6.5 billion
item.description: i-nest capital completed fundraising for its second fund, lifting assets under management for the vehicle to about JPY 6.5 billion. The fund first closed on
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: i-nest capital completed fundraising for its second fund, lifting assets under management for the vehicle to about JPY 6.5 billion. The fund first closed on Jan. 31, 2025; it has a 10-year term with an extension option of up to two years. Since the first close, the fund has invested in 11 startups as of Sept. 14, 2026. Its first fund was formed in December 2019 with JPY 7.3 billion; it backed 45 companies, generating 14 exits. A three-partner investment committee structure began in June 2026, with Tetsuya Nakajima joining as partner. item.title: Vividthree audited FY2026 net loss attributable to shareholders at S$9.15 million
item.description: Vividthree published audited FY2026 results showing higher revenue of S$ 1.87 million versus unaudited S$ 1.72 million. Gross profit rose to S$ 984,000 from
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vividthree published audited FY2026 results showing higher revenue of S$ 1.87 million versus unaudited S$ 1.72 million. Gross profit rose to S$ 984,000 from S$ 739,000, reflecting audit-driven revenue recognition adjustments. Net loss attributable to equity holders narrowed to S$ 9.15 million from S$ 9.45 million. Contract liabilities fell to S$ 14,000 from S$ 261,000, linked to the same revenue recognition changes. Derivative financial instrument liability was revised to S$ 1,000 from S$ 23,000 following year-end fair value measurement. item.title: Atmos Energy forecasts 6%-8% annual EPS, dividend growth through fiscal 2030
item.description: Atmos Energy forecast 6%-8% annual EPS growth through fiscal 2030, supported by a safety-driven, regulated natural gas delivery strategy. Capital plan total
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Atmos Energy forecast 6%-8% annual EPS growth through fiscal 2030, supported by a safety-driven, regulated natural gas delivery strategy. Capital plan totals USD 26 billion through 2030, with more than 85% allocated to safety and reliability projects. Rate-base outlook implies growth from USD 18.8 billion in FY2025 to USD 42 billion by FY2030E. EPS outlook shows USD 8.40-8.50 for FY2025, USD 10.80-11.20 for FY2026E, USD 11.20 by FY2030E. Recovery assumptions include earning on over 90% of annual capex within 6 months, about 99% within 12 months. item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ISS set 2026-2028 targets for average annual organic growth above 5%, replacing guidance issued in November 2022. Operating margin before other items excl IAS 29 forecast at 5.5%-6% in 2028. Cash conversion expected above 60% over the period. Like-for-like growth expected to drive a larger share of organic growth, while pricing contributes less than in 2026. 2026 outlook reiterated unchanged from the H1 2026 interim report released Aug. 11, 2026. item.description: ISS set new 2026-2028 mid-term targets to lift organic growth and expand profitability. Plan calls for average annual organic growth above 5% across 2026-20
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ISS set new 2026-2028 mid-term targets to lift organic growth and expand profitability. Plan calls for average annual organic growth above 5% across 2026-2028. Aim for a 5.5%-6.0% operating margin in 2028. Target cash conversion above 60% over the period. Growth mix to tilt toward like-for-like gains, with a smaller contribution from price rises than in 2026.
